# Future R wrapper: CLI installation and CRAN checks

Status: design direction recorded on 2026-10-20, not a shipped wrapper or an
accepted CRAN submission. The existing R package remains untouched. This note
does not settle the complete frontend protocol or claim renderer parity.

## Separate installation

The future wrapper is intended to contain R code that calls a separately installed
proj CLI. It should discover a compatible executable and give an actionable
missing/incompatible-CLI error. A user-invoked installer on the user's own machine
is distinct from automatic downloads during CRAN installation, checks or examples.
Do not assume CRAN servers already provide proj.

[CRAN source-package policy](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/policies.html#Source-packages)
permits downloads of precompiled software only as a last resort with CRAN-team
agreement. A separate executable is not an automatic exemption. Review
[Writing R Extensions: portability](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Writing-portable-packages)
when implementing the package, including external software availability and
portable invocation. This work has neither requested nor obtained CRAN agreement;
no outreach is authorized here.

## Two complementary test environments

| Environment | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| CRAN, CLI absent | Always run meaningful R-only validation, argument construction, missing-CLI diagnostics and mocked protocol/response tests. Skip only genuine executable integration tests, explicitly because the CLI is unavailable. |
| CRAN, compatible CLI available | Run the applicable real integration tests as well as the R-only tests. Do not assume every check host supplies it. |
| Our integration CI | Install an exact pinned CLI release, verify its checksum and compatible version, and run real end-to-end tests. Missing CLI or failed installation is a failure, never a silent skip. |

Mocked responses check the wrapper contract; they do not prove the CLI or renderer
works. Our mandatory integration job supplies that evidence. Examples and vignettes
must also handle optional executable availability honestly instead of requiring
an undeclared download. A requirement to execute proj on CRAN check servers would
need an agreed deployment/checking arrangement, not an assumed policy exception.

## Relevant Quarto precedent

The pinned Quarto R package
[DESCRIPTION at v1.5.1](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-r/blob/v1.5.1/DESCRIPTION)
declares the separate Quarto command-line tool in SystemRequirements.
Its [test helper](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-r/blob/v1.5.1/tests/testthat/helpers.R)
can skip executable-dependent tests when Quarto is unavailable, and its
[vignette utility](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-r/blob/v1.5.1/R/utils-vignettes.R)
checks executable availability during vignette processing. These are specific
implementation precedents, not proof that CRAN has accepted a future proj wrapper
or guaranteed an executable on every server. This note does not infer automatic
binary-download permission from Quarto's existence.

Before implementation, specify compatible protocol versions, executable discovery,
argument quoting, diagnostics, and which tests are unconditional versus executable
integration. R production changes require separate authorization.
